assumptions: Freeze each finite observed classification, including records stopped by source coverage. Later reheating or larger peaks would invalidate this scenario.
Assume one connected strong-reheater interval locally and no missed positive or negative islands.
Place each edge halfway between its nearest positive and nonpositive sampled mass. This midpoint is a chosen interpolation, not a likelihood estimate.
The endpoint width range varies the two edges over those assumed sample intervals. It is neither a confidence interval nor a physical error bound.
The 10percent rise criterion defines this strong-rise scenario; a different amplitude threshold defines a different interval.
Legacy solar/enriched and new low-Z models have different material, atmosphere, mesh and evolution assumptions. Their comparison is not a controlled metallicity derivative.
Rows without a positive sample stay unknown. No zero width is assigned to PopIII and trace-metallicity rows.
These scenarios guide the next sparse samples. They do not replace null measured widths in the authoritative outcome ledger.
All seven halfsolar birth configurations match except mass; spatial and source convergence remain unestablished.

The lower outward control remains source-limited at121.853Gyr and the upper outward control is fully connected through300Gyr. Their finite classifications are assumed to persist for this first-look interpolation.
Both new midpoints exceed the 10 percent delayed-temperature-rise threshold. Their stops at 131.479 and 262.650 Gyr do not establish peaks or completed requested ages.
Five discrete positives are treated as one connected band for interpolation only. The conditional endpoint range is neither a confidence interval nor a physical error bound.
